  You are revising ADR-0015 at D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0015-integer-kinematics-and-the-ship-body.md (project D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d, Godot 4.7.2 GDScript) after per-ADR engine and TD-ADR reviews and a cross-ADR adjudication of the Core tier.   ADR-0015 review verdict CONCERNS (engine review, Godot 4.7.2). No hard blocker. The core engine decisions hold up on 4.7.2 and need no changes:
  - no engine physics on any sim path;
  - id-sorted SoA columns held in PackedInt32Array and PackedInt64Array;
  - `@abstract` ports, including the one-line `@abstract class_name X extends RefCounted` form (probed to parse and instantiate);
  - the typed-return override rule, which the ADR already applies;
  - the packed-array element-write change, which the ADR does not rely on (probed: 0 setter calls).
  
  Three things need amendment before Accepted. A literal reading of the ADR yields a hot-path lint failure (E1), a non-compiling constant (E2), and a restore that silently wraps out-of-range int32 values (E3). A forward-reference mismatch with ADR-0014 is listed in cross_adr.
  
  Probe results (4.7.2.stable.mono, headless, in adr-probes/review-ADR-0015):
  - V1 reproduced: `bsearch` insertion index exact for 2^53+7, `insert`, `remove_at`, `duplicate()` independence, `b = a` aliasing.
  - V2 partly reproduced: truncating `/` and `posmod`. The literal -181/256 and -768/256 values were not re-run.
  - V3 reproduced: 2^23+1 round-trips through `Node2D.position`, 2^24+1 collapses to 16777216.
  - V4 (300,000-fixture equivalence) and V5 to V8 (GDScript cost, SoA versus records, release export, `reparent`) were not re-run by me. V8 is answered in cross_adr.
  - The 2.4 versus 23.8 microsecond figures are plausible: a bare packed-array read in a loop costs about 14 ns here.:
  E1 [medium] `collide.bind(body_id)` is called inside `BodyModule._hook_integrate`, which the ADR tags `## @hot`. ADR-0010 HOT-01 bans the token `.bind(` (as `Callable.bind`), and § 5.1 and § 7 repeat that ban. The lexical scan cannot tell a port method from `Callable.bind`, so the ADR's own hook fails BDY-06/HOT-01 as written. No Object or RefCounted method named `bind` exists (probed), so it is a lint clash, not an engine clash. It is also redundant: ADR-0014's `solid_in` takes `body_id` per call.
    amendment: Rename the port method to `bind_body(body_id)` or drop it and pass `body_id` to `query_into` and `origin_in_body` (matches ADR-0014). Update § 5.1, § 7, the Key Interfaces block, and the `CountingCollide` wording. Do not carve a HOT-01 exemption.
  E2 [medium] § 2 says `LocomotionTables` holds `UNIT_X[8]`, `UNIT_Y[8]` and `ODO_W[8]` as constants, but gives no declaration form. The obvious form `const UNIT_X := PackedInt32Array([256, 181, ...])` does not compile on 4.7.2: probed, "Assigned value for constant isn't a constant expression". `const A = PackedInt32Array()` fails the same way. These forms work: `const A: PackedInt32Array = [256, 181, ...]` (probed: typeof is TYPE_PACKED_INT32_ARRAY), `const A: Array[int] = [...]`, and `static var` with a constructor. `Vector2i(...)` consts also work. The ADR's other consts (int expressions such as `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`, and `const NAMES: Array[StringName] = [&"", &"X"]`) compile (probed).
    amendment: In § 2 and the Key Interfaces block, state the form: `const UNIT_X: PackedInt32Array = [..]` (or `Array[int]`), never `PackedInt32Array([..])` in a `const`. Add a one-line load test for `LocomotionTables` to the golden test. Note that a const array is read-only, so the hot path only reads it.
  E3 [medium] Writing an int into a PackedInt32Array element wraps silently with no error or warning. Probed: `a[0] = 1<<31` gives -2147483648 and `a[1] = (1<<32)+5` gives 5. NARROWING_CONVERSION does not fire for int to int. § 11.2 step 4 range-checks `sub`, `octant`, `odometer`, `heading` and the pose, but not `pos_x`/`pos_y`, `body_id`, or `seat` (only `>= 0`). § 4.1 stores these in int32 columns, and `kind` is only checked against two values. A decoded payload with a value at or above 2^31 would pass Phase 1, wrap in Phase 2, and break the claims 'first failure wins' and `snapshot(restore(x)) == x`. The same hole exists in the mutator arguments `x`, `y`, `shift_*`, `seat` and `to_body_id`.
    amendment: Add a Phase 1 rule: every value destined for an int32 column must lie inside explicit bounds (`body_id` 1..2^31-1, `seat` 0..MAX_SEAT, `pos_*` within a stated body-frame limit, shifts within it), failing with a new local code `BDY_RESTORE_COLUMN_RANGE` (append-only, domain 5 local 33) or an existing one. Mirror the bounds in `can_place`, `can_transfer` and `can_rebase_*`, so apply-time never writes an out-of-range int32. Add a MUT-CONS/BODY-RT fixture with 2^31 and 2^32+5.
  E4 [low] § 4 says 'row = bsearch position' but never says how absence is detected. `PackedInt64Array.bsearch(v)` always returns an insertion index (probed: `bsearch(2)` on [1,3,2^53+7] returns 1; `bsearch(3, false)` on a present value returns 2 and the default `before=true` returns 1). A row for an absent id can therefore be `size()`, and an unchecked `a_id[row]` read is out of range. In a release export that read logs an error and yields 0. That is exactly the 'stale row' failure R10 worries about, and it is not caught by 'no cached index'. The § 11.3 getters (`pos_x(actor)` etc.) and BM2/BM5 on an unknown actor are the exposed paths.
    amendment: Specify a single private `_find_actor_row(id) -> int` returning -1 unless `row < a_id.size() and a_id[row] == id` (same for bodies), with `before=true`. All getters return a neutral value on -1 and mutators return `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR`. Add a unit test for absent ids at the first, middle, last and past-the-end positions.
  E5 [low] The § 7 pseudocode `blocked[i] := result.blocked` (a `bool` into `BodyDerived.a_blocked: PackedByteArray`) is invalid GDScript. Probed on 4.7.2: "Invalid assignment of property or key '0' with value of type 'bool' on a base object of type 'PackedByteArray'". It would fail at load or error every tick inside the hook.
    amendment: State `a_blocked[i] = 1 if r.blocked else 0` in § 7, and read it as `a_blocked[i] != 0` in `BodyView.blocked`. This is allocation-free and HOT-01 clean.
  E6 [low] ADR-0010 sets SHADOWED_VARIABLE, SHADOWED_VARIABLE_BASE_CLASS, SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER and UNUSED_PARAMETER to 2 (error). Probed with those at 2: a parameter named like an existing member fails ("local function parameter 'collide' is shadowing an already-declared variable"), and an unused parameter fails ("never used ... prefix it with an underscore"). `BodyModule.setup(facet, tuning, collide, layout, sink)` injects ports that the module stores in members. The natural member names `collide`, `layout`, `sink`, `tuning` would shadow the parameters. `snap_baseline(key, ctx)` deliberately ignores `key`, and `_hook_integrate(views, scope, ctx)` is similar. Test doubles of the ports ignore arguments.
    amendment: Add to Implementation Guidelines: stored ports are private members (`_collide`, `_layout`, `_sink`, `_tuning`); every intentionally unused kernel-signature or double parameter is underscore-prefixed (`_key`). Show `snap_baseline(_key: int, ctx: ...)` in § 8.
  E7 [low] § 11.2 phase 2 says columns are 'assigned from the scratch's own arrays' while 'the object is never replaced'. Assigning `state.a_x = scratch_a_x` replaces the packed array reference and makes the live column alias the scratch (probed: a write through `scratch` is visible in `state.a_x`, and a pre-existing alias keeps the old data). The facade survives because BodyState is the same object, but any cached column alias is stale, and a retained scratch aliases live state. `PackedInt32Array.assign()` does not exist on 4.7.2 (probed), so it cannot be the 'copy in place' fix.
    amendment: Say restore builds the scratch as fresh locals discarded after phase 2 (never a member), or does `resize` plus an element copy loop (cold path). Forbid caching a packed column in any member of `BodyView`, the hook, or `LayoutCollide` (loop-local aliases only, as § 7 already says), and add a test that restores and then reads through a pre-held view.
  E8 [low] The § 1 additions to the SIM-06/BDY-01 token list are incomplete for 2D physics. Missing entries that can answer collision or overlap questions on a sim path: `RayCast2D`, `ShapeCast2D`, `KinematicCollision2D`, `PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D`, `PhysicsPointQueryParameters2D`, `PhysicsDirectBodyState2D`, `CollisionObject2D`, `CollisionShape2D`, `CollisionPolygon2D`, `direct_space_state`, `get_world_2d`, and the TileMapLayer `collision_enabled` property. Most are Node subclasses, so SIM-01 may catch them only by exact name.
    amendment: Add those tokens to the BDY-01 list in § 1 and § 12, and to the ask to ADR-0010. Note that the engine's 2D physics server still exists and ticks with no bodies (harmless), so the guarantee is 'no use', not 'not instantiated'.
  E9 [info] § 11.1 uses plain bare `Array` payloads and `typeof` walks over a Variant tree. ADR-0010 SIM-09 bans bare `Array`/`Variant` in `src/sim`, and snapshot code needs an `dictionary_variant.json`-style allow-list entry that the ADR does not request. The justification 'the type walk still needed on the JSON path' is moot: ADR-0006 § 1.3 says the JSON dump is diagnostics only, never a load path (and `JSON.parse` yields floats for all numbers, so ints could not round-trip anyway). The typed-versus-untyped alternative is also not engine-blocked, since ADR-0005 encodes typed and untyped arrays identically.
    amendment: Add to the ADR-0010 asks: an allow-list entry for `body_state` snapshot/restore code (bare `Array`, `Variant`). Reword the Alternative 10 and § 11.1 rationale to the binary path only.
  E10 [info] Notes on the probed claims. V3 reproduced (8388609 and -8388609 round-trip; 16777217 becomes 16777216). Exact integer representability of `Node2D.position` is not sub-pixel precision: at 2^22 the float32 ulp is 0.5 px and at 2^23 it is 1 px. The `floor()` in `canvas_offset_render` is therefore load-bearing, not cosmetic, and an unfloored interpolation at large offsets would quantise. `>>` on a negative literal is a parse error ("Only positive operands are supported"), while a negative variable shifts arithmetically at runtime (-5 >> 1 = -3, probed), so the ADR's only use (`FOOT_BOX_W >> 1`, positive and boot-checked even) is safe. `Array`/`posmod`/`mini`/`maxi`/`absi`/`signi`/`clampi` exist with int returns.
    amendment: In § 10, state that `canvas_offset_render` must floor before assigning to `Node2D.position` and that `>>` must never receive a negative operand in `src/sim/body/`. Keep the release-export repeat of V2/V3 as already planned.
  
  ADR-0015 review verdict CONCERNS:
  T1 [high, BLOCKING] BM3's apply-time predicate cannot pass on a real weld. § 9 BM3 checks that 'both [ids] live in Layout (BDY_REBASE_UNKNOWN_BODY)', and the check-then-write rule re-evaluates the whole predicate at apply time. But the mandated order inside the apply is Graph, then Layout, then Body, and ADR-0013 § 7 LM2 'mark[s] the absorbed body DISSOLVED' before BM3 runs. If body_is_live (ADR-0015's own ask to ADR-0013) means state == LIVE, every weld faults at BM3 and the scope closes after the Graph and Layout have already applied. That is the R5 no-rollback state on the happy path.
    amendment: Split BM3's predicate by phase. can_rebase_attach (called in validate, before LM2) requires both bodies to be LIVE. rebase_on_attach (apply, after LM2) requires: surviving is LIVE; absorbed is DISSOLVED in Layout; body_of(s) == surviving for every section that was on absorbed. Define body_is_live as state == LIVE in the BodyLayoutPort comment, add a Layout read body_state(body_id) (LIVE/DISSOLVED/UNKNOWN) or a body_was_absorbed_into(absorbed, surviving) read, and add a MUT-CONS case that runs LM2 then BM3 against the real Layout double.
  T2 [high, BLOCKING] No Body path exists for a body that Layout dissolves outside a weld. ADR-0013 LM4 discard_section_geometry (Web Map only) marks the section's body DISSOLVED. Body then keeps its pose row and any actor rows on that body. The hook tolerates them (BDY_ORPHAN_ACTOR), but restore step 6 rejects them (BDY_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BODY), so the next autosave becomes unloadable. That is the same failure the ADR calls load-bearing for BM4 saturation. I3 ('every body_id live in Layout') is claimed after every Body call, but a Layout mutator breaks it without any Body call. The obvious workaround (BM2 per actor plus BM6/BM7 zeroing before LM4) contradicts the § 9 rule that Body mutators run after the Layout mutator, and BM6/BM7 called after LM4 fault with *_UNKNOWN_BODY.
    amendment: Add BM8 release_body(scope, body_id) -> int with can_release_body(views, body_id) -> StringName: it refuses (reason BDY_RELEASE_ACTORS_PRESENT) while any actor row is on the body, and otherwise deletes the pose row. It runs after LM4 in the same apply, and its predicate accepts a DISSOLVED body. State the discard sequence for ADR-0026: transfer or remove actors (BM5/BM2) before LM4, then LM4, then BM8. Restate I3 as an invariant of the whole apply, and add LM4 to the MUT-CONS generator. Alternatively, have restore skip and count orphan rows; the T2 fix above is preferred because it keeps the restore strict.
  T3 [high, BLOCKING] The Layout seam does not match the sibling ADR-0014, which now exists in the same wave. ADR-0014 § 5 publishes SolidQuery.solid_in(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out) (not solid_in_into). Its QueryBuffer (§ 4) has columns keys, spans and flags, where spans holds four ints per record (x0, y0, x1 - 1, y1 - 1): inclusive occupied spans, not half-open x0/y0/x1/y1. ADR-0014 also assumes 'LocomotionStep takes a SolidQuery and passes the actor's body_id', but ADR-0015 defines its own CollideSource with a stateful bind(). § 5.1's escape clause ('LayoutCollide absorbs the difference') is wrong, because AxisClamp reads the QueryBuffer directly. A story written from § 5.3 (r.x1 half-open) against ADR-0014's spans would be off by one pixel, and actors would sink one pixel into walls; SWEEP-EQ only catches this if the oracle uses the same decode.
    amendment: Rewrite § 5.1 and the Key Interfaces against ADR-0014 verbatim. LayoutCollide wraps SolidQuery.solid_in. AxisClamp reads out.spans[4i .. 4i+3] and uses r.x1 = spans[4i+2] + 1 and r.y1 = spans[4i+3] + 1 through one inline helper. SweepOracle and the test double use the same decode, and one fixture covers a 1-px-wide leaf. Replace bind(body_id) with an explicit body_id argument on query_into and origin_in_body, matching ADR-0014 § 5's 'explicit body_id, no per-body handle' rationale. Close OQ-2 (ADR-0014 answers 'coordinates' via spans). State that CollideSource is a Body-side port that wraps SolidQuery plus section_at, and have ADR-0014's assumption line say so. Add ADR-0014's @abstract release fallback (LINT-SPIKE-1(a)) to Engine Compatibility.
  T4 [medium, BLOCKING] The sub reset on transfer is stated inconsistently inside the ADR. The Shared table row for TR-pc-035 says '§ 9 BM3/BM4/BM5 reset pos_prev and sub in P2'. But § 9 BM3 keeps sub and last_octant (as TR-shipbody-023 requires), and BM3 changes body_id for every absorbed-body actor, which is exactly the 'change of body_of_actor' that TR-pc-035 says resets sub. ADR-0019's assumption on ADR-0015 repeats the wrong reading ('BM3 weld, BM4 detach, BM5 pod hop reset pos_prev == pos_curr and sub'). A story would embed whichever sentence it reads first.
    amendment: Correct the TR-pc-035 row. All three mutators set pos_prev := pos_curr. BM4 (new side) and BM5 zero sub. BM3 keeps sub by TR-shipbody-023, because a whole-pixel 24-grid shift cannot disturb a residue. Record that TR-pc-035's 'resets sub' is read as covering a pod hop and a detach only, and ask that the TR text be amended. Add a BM3 property test showing sub and last_octant are byte-identical before and after.
  T5 [medium] BM4 step (4) 'creates the new pose row' without applying the sparse rule of § 4.1. If world_old + shift == (0, 0) and vel_old == (0, 0) (for example, an old body at world (-576, -96) cut at a section whose offset_old is (576, 96)), the row is canonical-empty. Restore then rejects it as BDY_RESTORE_NONCANONICAL, which makes the next autosave unloadable. MUT-CONS's I2 would catch this only if the generator produces that case. Separately, the § 7 hook line 'if world == 0 and vel == 0 the row becomes canonical-empty: delete it' sits inside the freeze branch, which is unreachable because |vel| <= 16 cannot overflow from world 0.
    amendment: In BM4 (4): 'insert the row only if it is not canonical-empty; otherwise the new body is the sparse zero'. Give MUT-CONS a directed case for this. Move the canonical-empty deletion in § 7 to after any write that can produce (0, 0, 0, 0), or delete the dead line.
  T6 [medium] LocomotionTables declares UNIT_X[8], UNIT_Y[8] and ODO_W[8] with OCTANT_NONE = 8. But § 6 step 3 evaluates UNIT_X[o] * v unconditionally, with o = NONE whenever v_eff == 0, and step 6 evaluates ODO_W[o] after the step-4 early exit. In GDScript, index 8 of an 8-element const array is a runtime error inside the hot hook. 'Or nothing when already at rest' in § 7 implies a guard that the algorithm text does not contain.
    amendment: Either size the three tables at 9 with a zero NONE row (generated and golden-tested like the others), or make step 2.5 explicit: 'if o == NONE: set sub := 0 and last_octant := NONE, then return moved (0, 0) before step 3'. Add a fixture with v_eff == 0 and octant NONE on the hot form.
  T7 [medium] The performance budget conflicts with ADR-0014. ADR-0015 § 13 cites the whole hook at 0.05 ms per actor (0.4 ms for eight), with the solid_in query included. ADR-0014 (TR-section-016) budgets solid_in alone at P99 0.05 ms per actor and 0.6 ms aggregate for eight actors. The query budget therefore exceeds the whole-hook budget that contains it, and S1 cannot pass both as written.
    amendment: Split the hook budget explicitly: query (ADR-0014's figure) plus clamp, row copy and marking (Body's figure), with the aggregate restated. Or note that the 0.05 ms TR figure is per actor including the query, and ask ADR-0014 to restate its per-actor P99 as the query share. Record which document S1 reports against.
  T8 [medium] The bounds ledger omits the body-frame bound that a sibling depends on. ADR-0017 (I-BOUNDS, I-OVERFLOW, item 6 of its assumptions) takes BODY_COORD_LIMIT 'from ADR-0015's bounds ledger', and needs doubled relative values below 2^26. ADR-0015 only says body-frame coordinates are 'tens of thousands of px' and that int32 suffices, and body_bounds.lock.json records world_coord_limit, vel_max and max_actors only. The registry's canvas_coordinate_exactness stance also says ADR-0015 owns that bound if body-frame extents could exceed 2^24.
    amendment: Add BODY_COORD_LIMIT to BodyTuning and to the ledger (default derived from MAX_SECTIONS times the maximum template extent, at or below 2^24). Restore rejects |pos| above it (fold into BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE or a new append-only code). State that Layout's can_attach must keep offsets inside it (a must-repeat for ADR-0013). Also state the canvas bound |off| + |pos| < 2^23 that keeps x + 0.5 exact for ADR-0018's light origin; WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX satisfies it, but the ADR should say so.
  T9 [medium] GDD Requirements Addressed misses three rows whose Foundation-ADR notes explicitly defer the residue to 'the Body ADR', and which this ADR in fact decides. TR-shipbody-005 (body.state registration values; ADR-0003 marks it Partial and says 'Body ADR') is decided in § 3. TR-shipbody-011 (body.integrate divisor and after set; ADR-0003 Partial, 'left to Body ADR') is decided in § 3. TR-shipbody-027 (no-force clause 'belongs to Ship Body GDD/physics ADR'; the event payload loses tick and seat) is decided in § 10 and § 11.5. TR-shipbody-010 (post_restore contents, planned ADR-0016) is also decided in § 8 and § 11.2 without being listed. As written the matrix will keep showing these rows as Partial or Gap.
    amendment: Add TR-shipbody-005, -011 and -027 to the Shared table, with Body's half and the Foundation half named, and TR-shipbody-010 to 'Owned elsewhere' (ADR-0016) with this ADR's contribution. Add TR-shipbody-027's payload change (tick and seat dropped, frame_delta split) to the GDD/TR sync list.
  T10 [low] Two invariants cover one fact. ADR-0015 § 2 declares CONTENT_INVARIANT BODY_BROADPHASE_CELL (BROADPHASE_CELL_PX >= FOOT_BOX_W + VEL_STEP_MAX). ADR-0014, which owns TR-shipbody-037, already declares BROADPHASE_CELL_COUPLING with the stricter form max(FOOT_BOX_W, FOOT_BOX_H) + V_RUN, plus its bound test. Two boot checks with different formulas will diverge on a retune.
    amendment: Delete BODY_BROADPHASE_CELL and cite ADR-0014's BROADPHASE_CELL_COUPLING (BroadphaseCoupling.holds) as the single check. Keep BODY_FOOT_W_EVEN.
  T11 [low] Cap safety is only half-expressed in Body's checks. can_rebase_detach(views, old_body_id, shift_x, shift_y) does not take cap_rects, so a caller's validate cannot ask Body the question that BM4 will later answer with a terminal scope.fault (BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP after the Graph and Layout have applied). TR-shipbody-039 requires every cut origin to check it (PLAYER refused, SYSTEM deferred), but the sibling-assumption wording narrows the repeat to PLAYER cuts.
    amendment: Add cap_rects to can_rebase_detach (from detach_preview(seam_id).rects) and return BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP as a reason, so ADR-0021's validate calls one Body check for every origin. Cite TR-shipbody-039 in the ADR-0021 must-repeat, covering all cut origins: PLAYER refuse, SYSTEM defer.
  T12 [low] The evidence and the MVP subset are not durable or prioritised. The V4 equivalence probe (300,000 fixtures) and the V1/V2/V3 scripts live in a user Temp directory outside the repository, so the evidence behind the analytic-clamp decision is not reproducible by a reviewer. The ADR also introduces eight BDY lints, two lint config files, a bounds ledger, a debug cross-check mode and a CI soak for a single module, without marking which pieces are needed at the Body epic's first story versus later (ADR-0010 § 6.10 lands rules with their owner's first story).
    amendment: Commit sweep_probe.gd and p2.gd under prototypes/ or tests/support/ and cite the repo path. Add a short 'MVP-required' list (SIM-06 + BDY-01, BDY-02, BDY-05, SWEEP-EQ, BODY-RT, MUT-CONS) and mark BDY-07, BDY-08, the BODY_SWEEP_CHECK soak and the bounds ledger as landing with their first triggering story.
  T13 [low] Minor contract gaps and stale items. AGENT-kind rows have no intent source in the § 7 hook (unused at the MVP, but the hook must do something deterministic). The ADR-0002 § 4 'binding_source payload shape' ask is already answered by ADR-0016 § 6.2 (flat PackedInt64Array, ascending by (player_id, entity_id)). ADR-0019's 'pod-body test' and 'home_body' reads are disowned without naming an owner.
    amendment: State that an AGENT row is not stepped at the MVP (treated as v_eff 0, as an unbound seat is, and counted). Replace the ADR-0002 ask with a citation of ADR-0016 § 6.2. Name ADR-0026 as the owner of the pod-body and home-body reads in the ADR-0019 sibling bullet.
  
  CROSS-ADR RULINGS (binding):
  CT-02 owner ADR-0013 (align: ADR-0011, ADR-0014, ADR-0015): Merges 0011-review item 1 (second half), 0013-review items 2, 11 and 12 (T3), and the RoomSource half of the LayoutViews single-inheritance item. ADR-0013 owns the port signature and the four record types. `LayoutViews` cannot extend several ports. The setup order is circular: Layout is set up first and needs the Graph port, while the Graph's setup needs Layout's `RoomSource`. I checked ADR-0010 section 2: sim-to-sim imports are allowed in any direction at module granularity, so ports that point both ways create no import-matrix problem and nothing needs to move to `src/shared/`.
    amendment: ADR-0013 section 8 port: rename `check_instantiate(views, template_id)` to `check_instantiate_section(views, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int) -> StringName`. `can_build` calls it. Section 11 defines four caller-owned records in `src/sim/layout/views/`, following ADR-0014's QueryBuffer precedent: `SectionBases {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`; `OpeningRead {area, area_max, door_state}`; `SeamOpenings {count, opening_ids: PackedInt32Array preallocated to the template maximum}`; `SectionCounts {nodes, edges, comps, stub_count, tombstoned: bool, next_section_id}` (meaning fixed by CT-03). Section 11 also states: '`LayoutViews` extends `RefCounted` only. It is constructed inside `LayoutModule.setup` and lives for the whole process. Each port is satisfied by a small adapter that delegates to it, with the port's method names. # Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.
- **Helpers in `.claude/scripts/` emit observations, never verdicts.** A script
  that scores or judges will eventually contradict a mode or override it cannot
  see. (Cited by `artifact-check.sh` and `adr-dep-graph.sh`.)

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Godot Engine — Version Reference

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine Version** | Godot 4.7 |
| **Installed at pin time** | 4.7.2.stable.mono.official.ed1daf0bf (matches pin; probed 2026-10-25 at `C:/Users/dasbl/Documents/Godot/`). 4.6.2 standard is also installed, unused. |
| **Release Date** | June 2026 (latest patch: 4.7.2, August 2026) |
| **Project Pinned** | 2026-10-17 |
| **Last Docs Verified** | 2026-10-17 (release timeline and 4.7 changes); 2026-02-12 (4.4-4.6 content) |
| **LLM Knowledge Cutoff** | May 2025 |

## Knowledge Gap Warning

The LLM's training data likely covers Godot up to ~4.3. Versions 4.5, 4.6
and 4.7 were released after the cutoff and introduced significant changes that
the model does NOT know about; 4.4 came out shortly before it and may be thinly
covered. Always cross-reference this directory before suggesting Godot API calls.

## Installed-Version Gap Warning

The warning above is one-directional — it covers the **model** knowing less than
this pin. The reverse gap is real and `/setup-engine` §3 creates it deliberately
("pin the newer one and upgrade later"): this reference can sit **ahead of the
installed editor**, and an agent citing it correctly then emits APIs that do not
compile locally. **Check `Installed at pin time` above before trusting a
version-qualified claim** — `NOT DETERMINED` means the gap is unknown, not absent.

## Post-Cutoff Version Timeline

| Version | Release | Risk Level | Key Theme |
|---------|---------|------------|-----------|
| 4.5 | Sep 2025 | HIGH | Accessibility (AccessKit), variadic args, @abstract, shader baker, SMAA |
| 4.6 | Jan 2026 | HIGH | Jolt default, glow rework, D3D12 default on Windows, IK restored |
| 4.7 | Jun 2026 | HIGH | AreaLight3D, HDR output, Asset Store replaces the Asset Library, VirtualJoystick, Jolt soft-body and world-boundary changes, typed-return overrides |

## Before the Cutoff

4.4 (Mar 2025, Jolt option, FileAccess return types) predates the May 2025
cutoff; the Knowledge Gap Warning still applies to it.

Dates from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases, checked 2026-10-17:
4.4 Mar 3 2025, 4.5 Sep 15 2025, 4.6 Jan 26 2026, 4.7 Jun 18 2026, 4.7.2 Aug 18
2026. Migration guides and release notes: `breaking-changes.md` § Sources.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag
- [Consistency-check needs a confirming run](consistency-check-confirming-run.md) — owner+registry fixes leave leftovers in consumer GDDs; grep referenced_by docs, print patch counts

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
